exactness_argument: KIC_INDEX_CANON changes one call in the index build: the canonical key and shift of each stored state's two normal-basis roots, (canonical, shift) = lift_scan_wide(root) instead of canonical_selected(root). The stored states are computed before and independently of that call (the S3 roots of each folded state, in the same order), so they are equal byte for byte. Both canonicalizers return the least rotation of the 83-bit word and the least shift that reaches it (83 is prime, so a word other than 0 and all-ones has one such shift, and both return 0 for those two), so every insert into the table is the same (key, packed value) in the same order, and the slot array is equal word for word. Everything downstream (the target scan, the rank stage, the relation, the probe counts, the echelon and the factor-log table) reads only the stored states and the table. Checked: on a 9-orbit base in every mode and on 400,000 random and structured words (crate tests); on the full K600 index locally (layout digests); and on the runner by cPIX on every root of every point and by the layout-digest gate on every IC process.

expected_effect.note: about 3.5% end to end, from run 39214027289's kP/kPaa rank stage and cP / cPI cold means; an estimate from another run, not a claim, and not an input of the rule or the power check

gates: every scheduled row valid (exit 0, verified, schedule match, no memory event)

every IC process: lift_scan, Feistel, prefetch; the 16-byte compact table with 2^26 slots over the folded index (14,940,300 stored of 29,880,000 logical states); 29,878,182 table entries; logical-state blake3 and table-map digests equal B's (online.index_digest); stored-state and table-slot blake3 equal the frozen layout (online.layout_digest: the same stored states and the same table layout, byte for byte); one index digest set across every IC process; the arm's index canonicalizer and scan self-test mode recorded; no root bloom

per point: one scalar across every IC process (cold and rank) and rT, replayed as [d]G = Q in the pinned oracle
per point: one relation (point indices) and one probe count across every IC process on the point
Q0 (O1): cP, cPI, cPIT and cPIX give the archived Feistel relation and scalar with 1,987,852 probes

question: Does canonicalizing the root-index build with lift_scan (KIC_INDEX_CANON=lift) instead of the selected canonicalizer lower the END-TO-END cold cost (setup + index build + rank stage + linear algebra + one-target online) of the rank-probe n=83 K600 producer on new targets, with the stored states, the root table's layout, every relation, every probe count, every scalar and the factor-log table unchanged?

rank_stage_design.choice: shared: K = the mean over the rank blocks of each block's mean rank stage over kP and kPI; E2E(c) = K + mean cold(c); the same K in the numerator and the denominator of the primary
rank_stage_design.pooling: kP and kPI are pooled (attempt indices shared within a block) so that K is not taken from either arm alone; the sharing control checks the pooling on the run
rank_stage_design.secondary: E2E with each arm's own rank processes, (kP + cP) / (kPI + cPI), attempts paired
rank_stage_design.why: only the cold path changes. KIC_INDEX_CANON is read only by the index build: the stored states do not depend on it, and the table receives the same inserts in the same order, so the rank stage runs identical code over an identical index (gated here byte for byte: the stored-state and table-slot digests). A per-arm rank stage would add only the rank stage's process-to-process drift (about +-0.3% per process in run 39214027289, 87% of the end-to-end cost) to a ratio whose treatment is entirely in the cold term. The rank stage is still measured in this run, because the end-to-end cost needs it on this host (no number is imported from another run), and kPI checks on the runner that the candidate pipeline's own rank process, on a lift_scan-built index, gives B's factor-log table with the baseline's relations and probes
